do: Set leg stride to a 12-frame rhythm per step.
Dip pelvisY and headY to their lowest points on the contact 'down' pose to establish physical weight.
Oppose shouldersRotZ heavily against hipsRotZ to create structural balance and vitality.
Swing arm in a wide pendulum arc, peaking in width on the down position.
dont: Keep pelvisY flat and level, which causes a weightless floating effect.
Move arms and legs on the same side of the rig forward simultaneously.

do: Use scale squash to sharply compress the character downward for 4 frames of anticipation.
Trigger a spring enter to snap the body upward into maximum extension.
Use a slow_in action bias to beautifully cushion into the final extreme holding pose.
Couple the spring enter with a camera push to amplify the emotional hit.
dont: Animate linearly from the idle state directly into the shock expression.
Settle into a completely dead mathematical freeze after the spring resolves.

do: Extend leg stride duration to 24 or 32 frames per step with high knee bends.
Keep pelvisY relatively flat and level during the passing position to create a gliding, weightless tightrope illusion.
Delay headY explicitly so it trails behind the lateral drift of the body.
Ease in heavily (cushion) as the foot finally makes contact.
dont: Trigger fast spring enters or rigid snappy timing.
Bob pelvisY and headY up and down violently on the pass positions.

do: Compress leg stride timing strictly to 6 frames per step.
Apply elongated scale squash heavily on the fast lateral drift to simulate transparent motion blur.
Vigorously pump arm swing forward and backward to oppose the legs.
Drive pelvisY down aggressively on the contact frames for maximum impact.
dont: Use slow_in or slow_out cushioning between the run steps.
Let the arms dangle loosely or drift without intentional opposition to the legs.

do: Use continuous micro photo sway and minimal lateral drift to keep the character breathing and alive.
Offset the timing of stick-rig joints so headY drifts slightly later than pelvisY.
Use a slow_out action bias to ease imperceptibly out of the starting position.
dont: Freeze the rig perfectly static, which kills the illusion of life instantly.
Use sudden opacity pops or fast scale squashes.

do: Use a deep squat anticipation to store energy before the jump.
Launch upward with arms spreading wide in celebration.
Land softly with bent knees to absorb the impact.
Add a secondary fist-pump or head toss at the apex.
dont: Keep the arms pinned to the sides during the jump.
Land stiff-legged without any give in the knees.

do: Use sharp, snappy timing with fast-out bias for aggressive impact.
Squash the character down deeply in anticipation before lunging forward.
Drive shoulders forward and rotate the head down defensively.
Hold the final frame briefly to let the hit register.
dont: Use slow cushioning which kills the aggressive energy.
Keep the spine upright and rigid during the lunge.
